content: The David Lorenz Light Pollution Atlas (djlorenz.github.io) uses VIIRS NPP satellite data processed by Colorado School of Mines Earth Observation Group. It maps locations using a Light Pollution Index (LPI) = artificial brightness / natural sky brightness, where natural sky = 22.0 mag/arcsec2 (SQM). The color scale divides into Zones 0-7 with sub-zones a/b; LPI=1 means artificial light equals natural (critical boundary). Factor of 3 per zone step. Specific threshold values are visual/color-based, not published as exact nW/cm2 numbers on the website. The atlas emphasizes it measures zenith brightness specifically, not the subjective Bortle scale view which covers horizon-to-zenith.
